children: The 424.65-km pipeline will have a total capacity of 6.84 MMSCMD, including 1.71 MMSCMD of common carrier capacity
Indian Oil Corporation (Indian Oil) will invest Rs 2,449 crore to build and operate a natural gas pipeline connecting Kochi in Kerala with Thoothukudi in Tamil Nadu, the company said on Monday.
The 424.65-kilometre pipeline will pass through Kochi, Kanyakumari and Thoothukudi, and will have a total capacity of 6.84 million standard cubic metres per day (MMSCMD).
Of the total capacity, 1.71 MMSCMD will be designated as common carrier capacity, allowing other entities to use the pipeline subject to applicable regulations and capacity availability.
The investment comes as India expands its natural gas transmission infrastructure and connectivity as part of efforts to increase the use of gas in the country's energy mix.
The pipeline will connect gas infrastructure across southern India and is expected to support the transportation of natural gas between Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
The project will be developed and operated by Indian Oil as the company expands its gas transmission network.
